subject: English
description: English complete progression map — 11 year levels, 279 standards, 7 strands. Merged from 4 source files.

standards.title: Language, expressions and gestures
standards.description: Understand how language, facial expressions and gestures are used to interact with others when asking for and providing information, making offers, exclaiming, requesting and giving commands
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how language, facial expressions and gestures are used in different types of interaction.

standards.title: Language to justify preferences
standards.description: Explore language to provide reasons for likes, dislikes and preferences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explore language used to give reasons for likes, dislikes and preferences.

standards.title: Texts organised by purpose
standards.description: Explore how texts are organised according to their purpose, such as to recount, narrate, express opinion, inform, report and explain
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explore how texts are organised differently according to their purpose.

standards.title: Repetition, rhyme and rhythm
standards.description: Explore how repetition, rhyme and rhythm create cohesion in simple poems, chants and songs
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explore how repetition, rhyme and rhythm create cohesion in poems, chants and songs.

standards.title: Print and screen text features
standards.description: Understand how print and screen texts are organised using features such as page numbers, tables of content, headings and titles, navigation buttons, swipe screens, verbal commands, links and images
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how print and screen texts are organised using navigation and structural features.

standards.title: Simple sentences
standards.description: Understand that a simple sentence consists of a single independent clause representing a single event or idea
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand that a simple sentence is a single independent clause representing one event or idea.

standards.title: Word classes
standards.description: Understand that words can represent people, places and things (nouns, including pronouns), happenings and states (verbs), qualities (adjectives) and details such as when, where and how (adverbs)
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand the major word classes: nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs.

standards.title: Images contribute to meaning
standards.description: Compare how images in different types of texts contribute to meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students compare how images in different text types contribute to meaning.

standards.title: Learning area vocabulary
standards.description: Recognise the vocabulary of learning area topics
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise vocabulary associated with different learning area topics.

standards.title: Sentence boundary punctuation
standards.description: Understand that written language uses punctuation such as full stops, question marks and exclamation marks, and uses capital letters for familiar proper nouns
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand sentence boundary punctuation and capital letters for proper nouns.

standards.title: Segment phonemes in words
standards.description: Segment words into separate phonemes (sounds) including consonant blends or clusters at the beginnings and ends of words (phonological awareness)
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students segment words into separate phonemes including consonant blends and clusters.

standards.title: Manipulate phonemes in words
standards.description: Orally manipulate phonemes in spoken words by addition, deletion and substitution of initial, medial and final phonemes to generate new words (phonological awareness)
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students manipulate phonemes by addition, deletion and substitution to generate new words.

standards.title: Use vowels and blends to read
standards.description: Use short vowels, common long vowels, consonant blends and digraphs to write words, and blend these to read one- and two-syllable words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use short and long vowels, blends and digraphs to write words and read one- and two-syllable words.

standards.title: Letters represent multiple sounds
standards.description: Understand that a letter can represent more than one sound and that a syllable must contain a vowel sound
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand that letters can represent multiple sounds and that syllables require a vowel sound.

standards.title: Spell with common letter patterns
standards.description: Spell one- and two-syllable words with common letter patterns
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students spell one- and two-syllable words using common letter patterns.

standards.title: Read and write high-frequency words
standards.description: Read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students read and write an increasing number of high-frequency words.

standards.title: Grammatical morphemes and word families
standards.description: Recognise and know how to use grammatical morphemes to create word families
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use grammatical morphemes to create and recognise word families.

standards.title: Features indicate text purpose
standards.description: Discuss different texts and identify some features that indicate their purposes
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss different texts and identify features that indicate their purposes.

standards.title: Turn-taking and active listening
standards.description: Use interaction skills including turn-taking, speaking clearly, using active listening behaviours and responding to the contributions of others, and contributing ideas and questions
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use interaction skills including turn-taking, active listening and responding to others' contributions.

standards.title: Compare text types
standards.description: Describe some similarities and differences between imaginative, informative and persuasive texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students describe similarities and differences between imaginative, informative and persuasive texts.

standards.title: Read with phrasing and fluency
standards.description: Read decodable and authentic texts using developing phonic knowledge, phrasing and fluency, and monitoring meaning using context and grammatical knowledge
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students read texts with developing phrasing and fluency, monitoring meaning using context and grammar.

standards.title: Build literal and inferred meaning
standards.description: Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising and questioning when listening, viewing and reading to build literal and inferred meaning by drawing on vocabulary and growing knowledge of context and text structures
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use comprehension strategies to build literal and inferred meaning, drawing on vocabulary and knowledge of text structures.

standards.title: Create and edit written texts
standards.description: Create and re-read to edit short written and/or multimodal texts to report on a topic, express an opinion or recount a real or imagined event, using grammatically correct simple sentences, some topic-specific vocabulary, sentence boundary punctuation and correct spelling of some one- and two-syllable words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit short written and multimodal texts using simple sentences, topic vocabulary and sentence punctuation.

standards.title: Deliver structured presentations
standards.description: Create and deliver short oral and/or multimodal presentations on personal and learnt topics, which include an opening, middle and concluding statement; some topic-specific vocabulary and appropriate gesture, volume and pace
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and deliver short presentations with clear structure, topic vocabulary and appropriate gesture, volume and pace.

standards.title: Language and images create meaning
standards.description: Discuss how language and images are used to create characters, settings and events in literature by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors and illustrators
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss how language and images create characters, settings and events in literature.

standards.title: Connect literature to experience
standards.description: Discuss literary texts and share responses by making connections with students' own experiences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss literary texts and share responses connecting to their own experiences.

standards.title: Plot, character and setting
standards.description: Discuss plot, character and setting, which are features of stories
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss plot, character and setting as features of stories.

standards.title: Sound patterns in poetry
standards.description: Listen to and discuss poems, chants, rhymes and songs, and imitate and invent sound patterns including alliteration and rhyme
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss and imitate sound patterns including alliteration and rhyme in poems, chants and songs.

standards.title: Retell using plot and language
standards.description: Orally retell or adapt a familiar story using plot and characters, language features including vocabulary, and structure of a familiar text, through role-play, writing, drawing or digital tools
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students retell or adapt familiar stories using plot, characters, language features and structure.

standards.title: Language varies by context
standards.description: Investigate how interpersonal language choices vary depending on the context, including the different roles taken on in interactions
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students investigate how language choices vary according to context and roles in interaction.

standards.title: Language to appreciate and prefer
standards.description: Explore how language can be used for appreciating texts and providing reasons for preferences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explore how language is used to appreciate texts and give reasons for preferences.

standards.title: Texts organised by purpose
standards.description: Identify how texts across the curriculum are organised differently and use language features depending on purposes
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify how texts across the curriculum are organised differently depending on purpose.

standards.title: Cohesion through pronouns
standards.description: Understand how texts are made cohesive by using personal and possessive pronouns and by omitting words that can be inferred
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how pronouns and ellipsis create cohesion in texts.

standards.title: Navigate print and screen texts
standards.description: Navigate print and screen texts using chapters, tables of contents, indexes, side-bar menus, drop-down menus or links
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students navigate print and screen texts using structural and navigation features.

standards.title: Compound sentences
standards.description: Understand that connections can be made between ideas by using a compound sentence with 2 or more independent clauses usually linked by a coordinating conjunction
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how compound sentences connect ideas using coordinating conjunctions.

standards.title: Noun groups and verb groups
standards.description: Understand that in sentences nouns may be extended into noun groups using articles and adjectives, and verbs may be expressed as verb groups
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how nouns extend into noun groups and verbs into verb groups.

standards.title: Images multiply meaning
standards.description: Understand that images add to or multiply the meanings of a text
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand that images add to or multiply meaning in texts.

standards.title: Conscious vocabulary choices
standards.description: Experiment with and begin to make conscious choices of vocabulary to suit the topic
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students experiment with and begin to make conscious vocabulary choices to suit a topic.

standards.title: Capital letters and commas
standards.description: Recognise that capital letters are used in titles and commas are used to separate items in lists
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise how capital letters and commas are used in titles and lists.

standards.title: Manipulate complex sounds
standards.description: Manipulate more complex sounds in spoken words and use knowledge of blending, segmenting, phoneme deletion and phoneme substitution to read and write words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students manipulate complex sounds and use blending, segmenting and substitution to read and write words.

standards.title: Use vowel digraphs and clusters
standards.description: Use phoneme-grapheme (sound-letter/s) matches, including vowel digraphs, less common long vowel patterns, consonant clusters and silent letters when reading and writing words of one or more syllables, including compound words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use vowel digraphs, long vowel patterns, consonant clusters and silent letters to read and write multisyllabic words.

standards.title: Spelling patterns and morphemes
standards.description: Use knowledge of spelling patterns and morphemes to read and write words whose spelling is not completely predictable from their sounds, including high-frequency words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use spelling patterns and morphemes to read and write words with unpredictable sound-spelling relationships.

standards.title: Prefixes, suffixes and word families
standards.description: Build morphemic word families using knowledge of prefixes and suffixes
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students build morphemic word families using prefixes and suffixes.

standards.title: Similar topics in different texts
standards.description: Identify how similar topics and information are presented in different types of texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify how similar topics and information are presented differently across text types.

standards.title: Express and respond to opinions
standards.description: Use interaction skills when engaging with topics, actively listening to others, receiving instructions and extending own ideas, speaking appropriately, expressing and responding to opinions, making statements, and giving instructions
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use interaction skills to actively listen, extend ideas, express and respond to opinions and give instructions.

standards.title: Identify purpose and audience
standards.description: Identify the purpose and audience of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify the purpose and audience of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts.

standards.title: Read with fluency and self-correct
standards.description: Read texts with phrasing and fluency, using phonic and word knowledge, and monitoring meaning by re-reading and self-correcting
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students read with phrasing and fluency, monitoring meaning by re-reading and self-correcting.

standards.title: Build and monitor meaning
standards.description: Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring and questioning to build literal and inferred meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use comprehension strategies to build literal and inferred meaning across texts.

standards.title: Create texts for familiar audiences
standards.description: Create and edit short imaginative, informative and persuasive written and/or multimodal texts for familiar audiences, using text structure appropriate to purpose, simple and compound sentences, noun groups and verb groups, topic-specific vocabulary, simple punctuation and common 2-syllable words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit imaginative, informative and persuasive texts for familiar audiences using appropriate structure and language.

standards.title: Deliver presentations with purpose
standards.description: Create, rehearse and deliver short oral and/or multimodal presentations for familiar audiences and purposes, using text structure appropriate to purpose and topic-specific vocabulary, and varying tone, volume and pace
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create, rehearse and deliver short presentations for familiar audiences, varying tone, volume and pace.

standards.title: Characters and settings across contexts
standards.description: Discuss how characters and settings are connected in literature created by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors and illustrators
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss how characters and settings are connected in literature from diverse contexts.

standards.title: Identify features and preferences
standards.description: Identify features of literary texts, such as characters and settings, and give reasons for personal preferences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify features of literary texts and give reasons for personal preferences.

standards.title: Language presents characters and settings
standards.description: Discuss the characters and settings of a range of texts and identify how language is used to present these features in different ways
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss how language presents characters and settings differently across texts.

standards.title: Experiment with sound patterns
standards.description: Identify, reproduce and experiment with rhythmic sound and word patterns in poems, chants, rhymes or songs
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify, reproduce and experiment with rhythmic sound and word patterns.

standards.title: Adapt structures and language features
standards.description: Create and edit literary texts by adapting structures and language features of familiar literary texts through drawing, writing, performance and digital tools
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit literary texts by adapting structures and language features of familiar texts.

standards.title: Social conventions and turn-taking
standards.description: Understand that cooperation with others depends on shared understanding of social conventions, including turn-taking language, which vary according to the degree of formality
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how cooperation depends on shared social conventions that vary with formality.

standards.title: Language of evaluation and emotion
standards.description: Understand how the language of evaluation and emotion, such as modal verbs, can be varied to be more or less forceful
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how evaluative and emotive language including modal verbs can vary in forcefulness.

standards.title: Text language features by purpose
standards.description: Describe how texts across the curriculum use different language features and structures relevant to their purpose
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students describe how language features and structures in curriculum texts vary according to purpose.

standards.title: Paragraphs group information
standards.description: Understand that paragraphs are a key organisational feature of the stages of written texts, grouping related information together
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how paragraphs group related information within stages of written texts.

standards.title: Layout and navigation features
standards.description: Identify the purpose of layout features in print and digital texts and the words used for navigation
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify the purpose of layout and navigation features in print and digital texts.

standards.title: Clauses with subject-verb agreement
standards.description: Understand that a clause is a unit of grammar usually containing a subject and a verb that need to agree
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand that clauses contain subjects and verbs that must agree.

standards.title: Verb types and processes
standards.description: Understand how verbs represent different processes for doing, feeling, thinking, saying and relating
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how different verb types represent doing, feeling, thinking, saying and relating.

standards.title: Verbs anchored in tense
standards.description: Understand that verbs are anchored in time through tense
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand that verbs are anchored in time through tense.

standards.title: Images extend meaning
standards.description: Identify how images extend the meaning of a text
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify how images extend the meaning of a text.

standards.title: Topic and technical vocabulary
standards.description: Extend topic-specific and technical vocabulary and know that words can have different meanings in different contexts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students extend topic-specific vocabulary and understand that words can have different meanings in different contexts.

standards.title: Apostrophes for contraction and possession
standards.description: Understand that apostrophes signal missing letters in contractions, and apostrophes are used to show singular and plural possession
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how apostrophes signal contractions and possession.

standards.title: Multisyllabic words and phonemes
standards.description: Understand how to apply knowledge of phoneme-grapheme (sound-letter) relationships, syllables, and blending and segmenting to fluently read and write multisyllabic words with more complex letter patterns
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students apply phoneme-grapheme knowledge and syllable patterns to fluently read and write multisyllabic words.

standards.title: Base words, prefixes and suffixes
standards.description: Understand how to apply knowledge of common base words, prefixes, suffixes and generalisations for adding a suffix to a base word to read and comprehend new multimorphemic words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students apply knowledge of base words, prefixes and suffixes to read and comprehend multimorphemic words.

standards.title: Less common letter patterns
standards.description: Use phoneme-grapheme (sound-letter) relationships and less common letter patterns to spell words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use phoneme-grapheme relationships and less common letter patterns to spell words.

standards.title: High-frequency words and homophones
standards.description: Recognise and know how to write most high-frequency words including some homophones
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise and write most high-frequency words including some homophones.

standards.title: Purpose and audience vary texts
standards.description: Recognise how texts can be created for similar purposes but different audiences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise how the same purpose can produce different texts when audiences differ.

standards.title: Share and extend ideas
standards.description: Use interaction skills to contribute to conversations and discussions to share information and ideas
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use interaction skills to contribute to conversations and discussions, sharing information and ideas.

standards.title: Identify audience and purpose
standards.description: Identify the audience and purpose of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts through their use of language features and/or images
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify audience and purpose of texts through their language features and images.

standards.title: Read accurately and fluently
standards.description: Read a range of texts using phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge to read accurately and fluently, re-reading and self-correcting when required
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students read a range of texts accurately and fluently using phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge.

standards.title: Evaluate texts with strategies
standards.description: Use comprehension strategies when listening and viewing to build literal and inferred meaning, and begin to evaluate texts by drawing on a growing knowledge of context, text structures and language features
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use comprehension strategies to build meaning and begin to evaluate texts using knowledge of context and structure.

standards.title: Plan, create and publish texts
standards.description: Plan, create, edit and publish imaginative, informative and persuasive written and multimodal texts, using visual features, appropriate form and layout, with ideas grouped in simple paragraphs, mostly correct tense, topic-specific vocabulary and correct spelling of most high-frequency and phonetically regular words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts using visual features, paragraphs and topic vocabulary.

standards.title: Deliver elaborated presentations
standards.description: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver short oral and/or multimodal presentations to inform, express opinions or tell stories, using a clear structure, details to elaborate ideas, topic-specific and precise vocabulary, visual features, and appropriate tone, pace, pitch and volume
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and deliver presentations using clear structure, elaborated details and precise vocabulary.

standards.title: Characters and events across contexts
standards.description: Discuss characters, events and settings in different contexts in literature by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors and illustrators
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss characters, events and settings across different cultural and contextual contexts in literature.

standards.title: Connect personal and character experiences
standards.description: Discuss connections between personal experiences and character experiences in literary texts and share personal preferences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss connections between their own experiences and those of literary characters.

standards.title: Language, setting and mood
standards.description: Discuss how an author uses language and illustrations to portray characters and settings in texts, and explore how the settings and events influence the mood of the narrative
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss how authors use language and illustrations to portray characters and explore how settings influence mood.

standards.title: Literary devices shape meaning
standards.description: Discuss the effects of some literary devices used to enhance meaning and shape the reader's reaction, including rhythm and onomatopoeia in poetry and prose
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss how literary devices including rhythm and onomatopoeia enhance meaning and shape reader response.

standards.title: Create using literary elements
standards.description: Create and edit imaginative texts, using or adapting language features, characters, settings, plot structures and ideas encountered in literary texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit imaginative texts using or adapting language features, characters, settings and plot structures.

standards.title: Language in formal and informal contexts
standards.description: Explore language used to develop relationships in formal and informal situations
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explore how language develops relationships in formal and informal situations.

standards.title: Subjective and objective language
standards.description: Identify the subjective language of opinion and feeling, and the objective language of factual reporting
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify subjective language of opinion and feeling versus objective language of factual reporting.

standards.title: Text stages and language features
standards.description: Identify how texts across the curriculum have different language features and are typically organised into characteristic stages depending on purposes
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify how curriculum texts have characteristic stages and language features depending on purpose.

standards.title: Text connectives and cohesion
standards.description: Identify how text connectives including temporal and conditional words, and topic word associations are used to sequence and connect ideas
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify how text connectives and topic word associations sequence and connect ideas.

standards.title: Online text navigation features
standards.description: Identify text navigation features of online texts that enhance readability including headlines, drop-down menus, links, graphics and layout
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify navigation features in online texts that enhance readability.

standards.title: Complex sentences
standards.description: Understand that complex sentences contain one independent clause and at least one dependent clause typically joined by a subordinating conjunction to create relationships, such as time and causality
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how complex sentences use subordinating conjunctions to create relationships between ideas.

standards.title: Direct and indirect speech
standards.description: Investigate how quoted (direct) and reported (indirect) speech are used
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students investigate how direct and indirect speech are used in texts.

standards.title: Adverb and prepositional phrases
standards.description: Understand how adverb groups/phrases and prepositional phrases work in different ways to provide circumstantial details about an activity
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how adverb groups and prepositional phrases provide circumstantial details.

standards.title: Past, present and future tense
standards.description: Understand past, present and future tenses and their impact on meaning in a sentence
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand past, present and future tenses and their impact on meaning.

standards.title: Image composition and framing
standards.description: Explore the effect of choices when framing an image, placement of elements in the image and salience on composition of still and moving images in texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explore how framing, element placement and salience affect composition in still and moving images.

standards.title: Synonyms and antonyms
standards.description: Expand vocabulary by exploring a range of synonyms and antonyms, and using words encountered in a range of sources
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students expand vocabulary by exploring synonyms and antonyms from a range of sources.

standards.title: Punctuation for dialogue
standards.description: Understand that punctuation signals dialogue through quotation marks and that dialogue follows conventions for the use of capital letters, commas and boundary punctuation
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how quotation marks and punctuation conventions signal and organise dialogue.

standards.title: Complex letter combinations
standards.description: Understand how to use and apply phonological and morphological knowledge to read and write multisyllabic words with more complex letter combinations, including a variety of vowel sounds and known prefixes and suffixes
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students apply phonological and morphological knowledge to read and write multisyllabic words with complex letter combinations.

standards.title: Spelling generalisations and origins
standards.description: Understand how to use knowledge of letter patterns, including double letters, spelling generalisations, morphological word families, common prefixes and suffixes, and word origins, to spell more complex words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use letter patterns, spelling generalisations, morphological families and word origins to spell complex words.

standards.title: Homophones and context spelling
standards.description: Read and write high-frequency words including homophones and know how to use context to identify correct spelling
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students read and write high-frequency words including homophones, using context to determine correct spelling.

standards.title: Texts across time and context
standards.description: Compare texts from different times with similar purposes and audiences to identify similarities and differences in their depictions of events
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students compare texts from different times to identify how context shapes depictions of events.

standards.title: Acknowledge and extend opinions
standards.description: Listen for key points and information to carry out tasks and contribute to discussions, acknowledging another opinion, linking a response to the topic, and sharing and extending ideas and information
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students listen for key points, acknowledge others' opinions and extend ideas in discussions.

standards.title: Identify characteristic features
standards.description: Identify the characteristic features used in imaginative, informative and persuasive texts to meet the purpose of the text
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify characteristic language features used in texts to meet their purpose.

standards.title: Integrate reading knowledge
standards.description: Read different types of texts, integrating phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge to read accurately and fluently, re-reading and self-correcting when needed
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students integrate phonic, semantic and grammatical knowledge to read different text types accurately and fluently.

standards.title: Evaluate and expand topic knowledge
standards.description: Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring and questioning to build literal and inferred meaning, to expand topic knowledge and ideas, and evaluate texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use comprehension strategies to build meaning, expand topic knowledge and evaluate texts.

standards.title: Publish with complex sentences
standards.description: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal imaginative, informative and persuasive texts, using visual features, relevant linked ideas, complex sentences, appropriate tense, synonyms and antonyms, correct spelling of multisyllabic words and simple punctuation
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create, edit and publish texts using complex sentences, linked ideas and appropriate vocabulary.

standards.title: Present arguments and recounts
standards.description: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver structured oral and/or multimodal presentations to report on a topic, tell a story, recount events or present an argument using subjective and objective language, complex sentences, visual features, tone, pace, pitch and volume
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and deliver structured presentations to report, recount or argue using complex sentences and voice features.

standards.title: Storylines across contexts
standards.description: Recognise similar storylines, ideas and relationships in different contexts in literary texts by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise similar storylines, ideas and relationships across texts from different cultural contexts.

standards.title: Describe text structure effects
standards.description: Describe the effects of text structures and language features in literary texts when responding to and sharing opinions
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students describe the effects of text structures and language features when responding to and sharing opinions.

standards.title: Character, setting and plot tension
standards.description: Discuss how authors and illustrators make stories engaging by the way they develop character, setting and plot tensions
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss how authors develop character, setting and plot tensions to make stories engaging.

standards.title: Literary devices and word play
standards.description: Examine the use of literary devices and deliberate word play in literary texts, including poetry, to shape meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students examine how literary devices and deliberate word play shape meaning in texts including poetry.

standards.title: Develop storylines and characters
standards.description: Create and edit literary texts by developing storylines, characters and settings
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit literary texts by developing their own storylines, characters and settings.

standards.title: Language signals social roles
standards.description: Understand that language is selected for social contexts and that it helps to signal social roles and relationships
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how language selection signals social roles and relationships.

standards.title: Beyond assertions to evidence
standards.description: Understand how to move beyond making bare assertions by taking account of differing ideas or opinions and authoritative sources
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how to move beyond bare assertions by incorporating differing views and authoritative sources.

standards.title: Text stages and phases
standards.description: Describe how spoken, written and multimodal texts use language features and are typically organised into characteristic stages and phases, depending on purposes in texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students describe how texts use language features and are organised into characteristic stages and phases.

standards.title: Starting point and prominence
standards.description: Understand how texts can be made cohesive by using the starting point of a sentence or paragraph to give prominence to the message and to guide the reader through the text
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how sentence and paragraph starting points create prominence and guide readers.

standards.title: Complex sentences for effect
standards.description: Understand that the structure of a complex sentence includes a main clause and at least one dependent clause, and understand how writers can use this structure for effect
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand complex sentence structure and how writers use it for effect.

standards.title: Expanded noun groups
standards.description: Understand how noun groups can be expanded in a variety of ways to provide a fuller description of a person, place, thing or idea
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how noun groups can be expanded to provide fuller descriptions.

standards.title: Image sequence and meaning
standards.description: Explain how the sequence of images in print, digital and film texts has an effect on meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how image sequences in print, digital and film texts affect meaning.

standards.title: Specialist vocabulary and word history
standards.description: Understand how vocabulary is used to express greater precision of meaning, including through the use of specialist and technical terms, and explore the history of words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how specialist vocabulary expresses precision and explore word history.

standards.title: Commas and apostrophes
standards.description: Use commas to indicate prepositional phrases, and apostrophes where there is multiple possession
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use commas to indicate prepositional phrases and apostrophes for multiple possession.

standards.title: Shared patterns, different sounds
standards.description: Use phonic, morphemic and vocabulary knowledge to read and spell words that share common letter patterns but have different pronunciations
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use phonic, morphemic and vocabulary knowledge to read and spell words with common patterns but different pronunciations.

standards.title: Build words from known patterns
standards.description: Build and spell new words from knowledge of known words, base words, prefixes and suffixes, word origins, letter patterns and spelling generalisations
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students build and spell new words using known words, base words, affixes, origins and spelling generalisations.

standards.title: Plurals and suffix effects
standards.description: Explore less common plurals, and understand how a suffix changes the meaning or grammatical form of a word
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explore less common plurals and explain how suffixes change meaning or grammatical form.

standards.title: Texts reflect time and place
standards.description: Describe the ways in which a text reflects the time and place in which it was created
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students describe how texts reflect the time and place of their creation.

standards.title: Paraphrase and justify opinions
standards.description: Use appropriate interaction skills including paraphrasing and questioning to clarify meaning, make connections to own experience, and present and justify an opinion or idea
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use paraphrasing and questioning to clarify meaning and present and justify opinions.

standards.title: Explain characteristic features
standards.description: Explain characteristic features used in imaginative, informative and persuasive texts to meet the purpose of the text
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how characteristic features in texts serve their purpose.

standards.title: Navigate texts for purpose
standards.description: Navigate and read texts for specific purposes, monitoring meaning using strategies such as skimming, scanning and confirming
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students navigate and read texts for specific purposes using skimming, scanning and confirming strategies.

standards.title: Evaluate information and ideas
standards.description: Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring and questioning to build literal and inferred meaning to evaluate information and ideas
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use comprehension strategies to build meaning and evaluate information and ideas across texts.

standards.title: Develop ideas with connectives
standards.description: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts whose purposes may be imaginative, informative and persuasive, developing ideas using visual features, text structure appropriate to the topic and purpose, text connectives, expanded noun groups, specialist and technical vocabulary, and punctuation including dialogue punctuation
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and publish texts developing ideas with connectives, expanded noun groups and specialist vocabulary.

standards.title: Deliver elaborated spoken presentations
standards.description: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations that include relevant, elaborated ideas, sequencing ideas and using complex sentences, specialist and technical vocabulary, pitch, tone, pace, volume, and visual and digital features
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and deliver presentations with elaborated, sequenced ideas and specialist vocabulary.

standards.title: Historical and cultural contexts
standards.description: Identify aspects of literary texts that represent details or information about historical, social and cultural contexts in literature by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify how literary texts represent historical, social and cultural contexts.

standards.title: Present opinion with literary terms
standards.description: Present an opinion on a literary text using specific terms about literary devices, text structures and language features, and reflect on the viewpoints of others
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students present opinions using specific literary terms and reflect on others' viewpoints.

standards.title: Point of view shapes response
standards.description: Recognise that the point of view in a literary text influences how readers interpret and respond to events and characters
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise how point of view influences reader interpretation and response.

standards.title: Imagery and sound devices
standards.description: Examine the effects of imagery, including simile, metaphor and personification, and sound devices in narratives, poetry and songs
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students examine the effects of imagery and sound devices in narratives, poetry and songs.

standards.title: Experiment with figurative language
standards.description: Create and edit literary texts, experimenting with figurative language, storylines, characters and settings from texts students have experienced
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit literary texts experimenting with figurative language and elements from experienced texts.

standards.title: Formality and social distance
standards.description: Understand that language varies as levels of formality and social distance increase
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how language varies with increasing formality and social distance.

standards.title: Objective, subjective language and bias
standards.description: Understand the uses of objective and subjective language, and identify bias
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand objective and subjective language and identify bias.

standards.title: Characteristic stages and adaptation
standards.description: Explain how texts across the curriculum are typically organised into characteristic stages and phases depending on purposes, recognising how authors often adapt text structures and language features
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain characteristic text stages and recognise how authors adapt structures and features.

standards.title: Cohesion through repetition
standards.description: Understand that cohesion can be created by the intentional use of repetition, and the use of word associations
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how repetition and word associations create cohesion in texts.

standards.title: Embedded clauses
standards.description: Understand how embedded clauses can expand the variety of complex sentences to elaborate, extend and explain ideas
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how embedded clauses expand complex sentences to elaborate and explain ideas.

standards.title: Verbs and adverbs for precision
standards.description: Understand how ideas can be expanded and sharpened through careful choice of verbs, elaborated tenses and a range of adverb groups
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how verb choice, elaborated tenses and adverb groups sharpen and expand ideas.

standards.title: Visual elements contribute to meaning
standards.description: Identify and explain how images, figures, tables, diagrams, maps and graphs contribute to meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify and explain how visual elements including images, tables and graphs contribute to meaning.

standards.title: Figurative and emotive vocabulary
standards.description: Identify authors' use of vivid, emotive vocabulary, such as metaphors, similes, personification, idioms, imagery and hyperbole
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify how authors use figurative and emotive vocabulary including metaphor, simile and hyperbole.

standards.title: Comma uses
standards.description: Understand how to use the comma for lists, to separate a dependent clause from an independent clause, and in dialogue
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how commas are used in lists, to separate clauses and in dialogue.

standards.title: Complex grapheme-phoneme patterns
standards.description: Use phonic knowledge of common and less common grapheme-phoneme relationships to read and write increasingly complex words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use phonic knowledge of grapheme-phoneme relationships to read and write increasingly complex words.

standards.title: Word origins and technical words
standards.description: Use knowledge of known words, word origins including some Latin and Greek roots, base words, prefixes, suffixes, letter patterns and spelling generalisations to spell new words including technical words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use word origins including Latin and Greek roots, affixes and spelling generalisations to spell new and technical words.

standards.title: Texts reflect context of creation
standards.description: Examine texts including media texts that represent ideas and events, and identify how they reflect the context in which they were created
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students examine how texts including media texts represent ideas and events to reflect their context of creation.

standards.title: Interrogate and evaluate ideas
standards.description: Use interaction skills and awareness of formality when paraphrasing, questioning, clarifying and interrogating ideas, developing and supporting arguments, and sharing and evaluating information, experiences and opinions
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use interaction skills with awareness of formality to interrogate ideas, develop arguments and evaluate opinions.

standards.title: Analyse structure and language
standards.description: Analyse how text structures and language features work together to meet the purpose of a text, and engage and influence audiences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how text structures and language features work together to meet purpose and influence audiences.

standards.title: Navigate and evaluate structure
standards.description: Select, navigate and read texts for a range of purposes, monitoring meaning and evaluating the use of structural features; for example, table of contents, glossary, chapters, headings and subheadings
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students select, navigate and read texts for varied purposes, evaluating structural features.

standards.title: Connect and compare sources
standards.description: Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring and questioning to build literal and inferred meaning, and to connect and compare content from a variety of sources
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use comprehension strategies to build meaning and connect and compare content across multiple sources.

standards.title: Publish complex varied texts
standards.description: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts whose purposes may be imaginative, informative and persuasive, using paragraphs, a variety of complex sentences, expanded verb groups, tense, topic-specific and vivid vocabulary, punctuation, spelling and visual features
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and publish varied texts using complex sentences, expanded verb groups and vivid vocabulary.

standards.title: Develop theme in presentations
standards.description: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations that include information, arguments and details that develop a theme or idea, organising ideas using precise topic-specific and technical vocabulary, pitch, tone, pace, volume, and visual and digital features
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and deliver presentations that develop a theme with precise vocabulary and digital features.

standards.title: Responses to historical contexts
standards.description: Identify responses to characters and events in literary texts, drawn from historical, social or cultural contexts, by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify responses to characters and events in texts drawn from historical, social or cultural contexts.

standards.title: Compare texts on similar topics
standards.description: Identify similarities and differences in literary texts on similar topics, themes or plots
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify similarities and differences in literary texts on similar topics, themes or plots.

standards.title: Author's individual style
standards.description: Identify and explain characteristics that define an author's individual style
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify and explain the characteristics that define an author's individual style.

standards.title: Sound and imagery in poetry
standards.description: Explain the way authors use sound and imagery to create meaning and effect in poetry
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how authors use sound and imagery to create meaning and effect in poetry.

standards.title: Adapt and experiment with literary devices
standards.description: Create and edit literary texts that adapt plot structure, characters, settings and/or ideas from texts students have experienced, and experiment with literary devices
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit literary texts adapting elements from experienced texts and experimenting with literary devices.

standards.title: Language and identity
standards.description: Understand how language expresses and creates personal and social identities
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how language expresses and creates personal and social identities.

standards.title: Evaluative language and substantiation
standards.description: Recognise language used to evaluate texts including visual and multimodal texts, and how evaluations of a text can be substantiated by reference to the text and other sources
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise evaluative language and understand how evaluations are substantiated by textual evidence.

standards.title: Text structure varies by purpose
standards.description: Identify and describe how texts are structured differently depending on their purpose and how language features vary in texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify and describe how text structure and language features vary by purpose.

standards.title: Cohesion devices guide readers
standards.description: Understand that the cohesion of texts relies on devices that signal structure and guide readers, such as overviews and initial and concluding paragraphs
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how cohesion devices including overviews and paragraph structure guide readers.

standards.title: Complex and compound-complex sentences
standards.description: Understand how complex and compound-complex sentences can be used to elaborate, extend and explain ideas
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how complex and compound-complex sentences elaborate, extend and explain ideas.

standards.title: Tense consistency
standards.description: Understand how consistency of tense through verbs and verb groups achieves clarity in sentences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how consistent tense through verbs and verb groups achieves clarity.

standards.title: Visual perspective techniques
standards.description: Analyse how techniques such as vectors, angle and/or social distance in visual texts can be used to create a perspective
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how vectors, angle and social distance in visual texts create perspective.

standards.title: Specialist and technical vocabulary
standards.description: Investigate the role of vocabulary in building specialist and technical knowledge, including terms that have both everyday and technical meanings
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students investigate how vocabulary builds specialist knowledge, including terms with everyday and technical meanings.

standards.title: Colons and brackets
standards.description: Understand the use of punctuation including colons and brackets to support meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how colons and brackets support meaning.

standards.title: Spelling rules and word origins
standards.description: Understand how to use spelling rules and word origins; for example, Greek and Latin roots, base words, suffixes, prefixes and spelling patterns to learn new words and how to spell them
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use spelling rules and word origins including Greek and Latin roots to learn and spell new words.

standards.title: Technology shapes text response
standards.description: Explain the effect of current technology on reading, creating and responding to texts including media texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how current technology affects reading, creating and responding to texts.

standards.title: Evaluate spoken text features
standards.description: Use interaction skills when discussing and presenting ideas and information including evaluations of the features of spoken texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use interaction skills to discuss and present ideas, evaluating features of spoken texts.

standards.title: Analyse language shaping meaning
standards.description: Analyse the ways in which language features shape meaning and vary according to audience and purpose
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how language features shape meaning and vary according to audience and purpose.

standards.title: Explain idea structures in texts
standards.description: Explain the structure of ideas such as the use of taxonomies, cause and effect, extended metaphors and chronology
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how ideas are structured using taxonomies, cause and effect, metaphors and chronology.

standards.title: Analyse and summarise ideas
standards.description: Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring, questioning and inferring to analyse and summarise information and ideas
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use comprehension strategies including inferring to analyse and summarise information and ideas.

standards.title: Select structures for purpose
standards.description: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts, selecting subject matter, and using text structures, language features, literary devices and visual features as appropriate to convey information, ideas and opinions in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive and/or analytical
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and publish texts selecting structures, language features and literary devices for purpose.

standards.title: Deliver purposeful presentations
standards.description: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver presentations for purposes and audiences in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive and/or analytical, by selecting text structures, language features, literary devices and visual features, and using features of voice including volume, tone, pitch and pace
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and deliver presentations selecting structures, devices and voice features for purpose and audience.

standards.title: Ideas and context in literature
standards.description: Identify and explore ideas, points of view, characters, events and/or issues in literary texts, drawn from historical, social and/or cultural contexts, by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify and explore ideas, viewpoints and issues in literary texts across historical, social and cultural contexts.

standards.title: Form and justify opinions
standards.description: Form an opinion about characters, settings and events in texts, identifying areas of agreement and difference with others' opinions and justifying a response
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students form and justify opinions about texts, identifying agreement and difference with others.

standards.title: Literary devices create character
standards.description: Explain the ways that literary devices and language features such as dialogue, and images are used to create character, and to influence emotions and opinions in different types of texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how literary devices and language features create character and influence emotions and opinions.

standards.title: Aesthetic and social value
standards.description: Discuss the aesthetic and social value of literary texts using relevant and appropriate metalanguage
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students discuss the aesthetic and social value of literary texts using appropriate metalanguage.

standards.title: Characters, settings and meaning
standards.description: Identify and explain the ways that characters, settings and events combine to create meaning in narratives
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify and explain how characters, settings and events combine to create meaning in narratives.

standards.title: Literary devices create layers
standards.description: Identify and explain how literary devices create layers of meaning in texts including poetry
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify and explain how literary devices create layers of meaning in texts including poetry.

standards.title: Experiment with language and devices
standards.description: Create and edit literary texts that experiment with language features and literary devices encountered in texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit literary texts experimenting with language features and literary devices.

standards.title: Language shapes relationships
standards.description: Recognise how language shapes relationships and roles
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise how language shapes relationships and roles.

standards.title: Literary devices in evaluation
standards.description: Understand how layers of meaning can be created when evaluating by using literary devices such as simile and metaphor
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how literary devices such as simile and metaphor create layers of meaning in evaluation.

standards.title: Hybrid text structures
standards.description: Explain how texts are structured depending on their purpose and how language features vary, recognising that some texts are hybrids that combine different genres or elements of different genres
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how text structure and language features vary by purpose and recognise hybrid genres.

standards.title: Paragraph cohesion with evidence
standards.description: Understand how cohesion in texts is improved by strengthening the internal structure of paragraphs with examples, quotations and substantiation of claims
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how paragraphs are made cohesive through examples, quotations and substantiated claims.

standards.title: Embedded clauses expand ideas
standards.description: Examine a variety of clause structures including embedded clauses that add information and expand ideas in sentences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students examine clause structures including embedded clauses that add information and expand ideas.

standards.title: Nominalisation
standards.description: Understand the effect of nominalisation in texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how nominalisation is used and its effect in texts.

standards.title: Intertextual references in visual texts
standards.description: Investigate how visual texts use intertextual references to enhance and layer meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students investigate how intertextual references in visual texts enhance and layer meaning.

standards.title: Academic vocabulary
standards.description: Identify and use vocabulary typical of academic texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify and use vocabulary typical of academic texts.

standards.title: Semicolons and dashes
standards.description: Understand and use punctuation conventions including semicolons and dashes to extend ideas and support meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand and use semicolons and dashes to extend ideas and support meaning.

standards.title: Apply spelling knowledge
standards.description: Apply learnt knowledge to spell accurately and to learn new words
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students apply accumulated spelling knowledge to spell accurately and acquire new words.

standards.title: Texts reflect contexts
standards.description: Identify how texts reflect contexts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify how texts reflect the contexts in which they were created.

standards.title: Challenge implied meanings
standards.description: Use interaction skills for identified purposes and situations, including when supporting or challenging the stated or implied meanings of spoken texts in presentations or discussion
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use interaction skills to support or challenge stated and implied meanings in spoken texts.

standards.title: Evaluate language and sources
standards.description: Analyse and evaluate the ways that language features vary according to the purpose and audience of the text, and the ways that sources and quotations are used in a text
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse and evaluate how language varies by purpose and audience, and how sources and quotations are used.

standards.title: Analyse idea organisation
standards.description: Analyse how authors organise ideas to develop and shape meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how authors organise ideas to develop and shape meaning.

standards.title: Interpret and evaluate ideas
standards.description: Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring, questioning and inferring to interpret and evaluate ideas in texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use comprehension strategies to interpret and evaluate ideas in texts.

standards.title: Organise and expand ideas
standards.description: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts, organising and expanding ideas, and selecting text structures, language features, literary devices and visual features for purposes and audiences in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive and/or analytical
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and publish texts organising and expanding ideas, selecting features for purpose and audience.

standards.title: Select features for formal contexts
standards.description: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations for audiences and purposes, selecting language features, literary devices, visual features and features of voice to suit formal or informal situations, and organising and developing ideas in texts in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive and/or analytical
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and deliver presentations selecting language and voice features for formal or informal situations.

standards.title: Values in historical contexts
standards.description: Explain the ways that ideas and points of view may represent the values of individuals and groups in literary texts, drawn from historical, social and cultural contexts, by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how ideas and viewpoints in literary texts represent the values of individuals and groups across contexts.

standards.title: Share opinions about style
standards.description: Share opinions about the language features, literary devices and text structures that contribute to the styles of literary texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students share opinions about how language features, literary devices and text structures contribute to literary style.

standards.title: Language positions readers
standards.description: Explain how language and/or images in texts position readers to respond and form viewpoints
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how language and images position readers to respond and form viewpoints.

standards.title: Intertextual references
standards.description: Identify intertextual references in literary texts and explain how the references enable new understanding of the aesthetic quality of the text
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify intertextual references and explain how they enable new aesthetic understanding.

standards.title: Sentence patterns and imagery
standards.description: Analyse how language features such as sentence patterns create tone, and literary devices such as imagery create meaning and effect
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how sentence patterns create tone and how literary devices create meaning and effect.

standards.title: Experiment for purposes and effects
standards.description: Create and edit literary texts that experiment with language features and literary devices for particular purposes and effects
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit literary texts experimenting with language features and devices for specific purposes and effects.

standards.title: Language empowers relationships
standards.description: Recognise how language empowers relationships and roles
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students recognise how language empowers relationships and roles.

standards.title: Indirect evaluation devices
standards.description: Understand how evaluation can be expressed directly and indirectly using devices such as allusion, evocative vocabulary and metaphor
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how evaluation is expressed directly and indirectly through allusion, vocabulary and metaphor.

standards.title: Adapting and subverting text structures
standards.description: Examine how authors adapt and subvert text structures and language features by experimenting with spoken, written, visual and multimodal elements, and their combination
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students examine how authors adapt and subvert text structures by experimenting with multimodal elements.

standards.title: Cohesion through nominalisation
standards.description: Investigate a range of cohesive devices that condense information in texts, including nominalisation, and devices that link, expand and develop ideas, including text connectives
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students investigate cohesive devices including nominalisation and text connectives that condense and link ideas.

standards.title: Creative sentence variation
standards.description: Identify how authors vary sentence structures creatively for effects, such as intentionally using a dependent clause on its own or a sentence fragment
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students identify how authors vary sentence structures creatively including deliberate fragments for effect.

standards.title: Abstract nouns and nominalisation
standards.description: Understand how abstract nouns and nominalisation can be used to summarise ideas in text
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how abstract nouns and nominalisation summarise ideas in texts.

standards.title: Symbols in visual texts
standards.description: Analyse how symbols in still and moving images augment meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how symbols in still and moving images augment meaning.

standards.title: Vocabulary for style and tone
standards.description: Analyse how vocabulary choices contribute to style, mood and tone
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how vocabulary choices contribute to style, mood and tone.

standards.title: Referencing and citation punctuation
standards.description: Understand punctuation conventions for referencing and citing others for formal and informal purposes
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand punctuation conventions for referencing and citing sources formally and informally.

standards.title: Spelling for stylistic effect
standards.description: Understand how spelling is used in texts for particular effects; for example, characterisation, humour and to represent accents and distinctive speech
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students explain how spelling is used deliberately in texts for effects such as characterisation, humour and accent representation.

standards.title: Representations reflect contexts
standards.description: Analyse how representations of people, places, events and concepts reflect contexts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how representations of people, places, events and concepts reflect their contexts.

standards.title: Analyse how language positions listeners
standards.description: Listen to spoken texts that have different purposes and audiences, analysing how language features position listeners to respond in particular ways, and use interacting skills to present and discuss opinions regarding these texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how language positions listeners and use interaction skills to present and discuss opinions about spoken texts.

standards.title: Evaluate perspective representation
standards.description: Analyse and evaluate how language features are used to represent a perspective of an issue, event, situation, individual or group
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse and evaluate how language features represent perspectives of issues, events and groups.

standards.title: Evaluate idea organisation
standards.description: Analyse the organisation of ideas in paragraphs and extended texts, and evaluate its impact on meaning
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse idea organisation in paragraphs and extended texts and evaluate its impact on meaning.

standards.title: Compare ideas across texts
standards.description: Use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring, questioning and inferring to compare and contrast ideas and opinions in and between texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students use comprehension strategies to compare and contrast ideas and opinions within and between texts.

standards.title: Develop critical written texts
standards.description: Plan, create, edit and publish written and multimodal texts, organising, expanding and developing ideas, and selecting text structures, language features, literary devices and multimodal features for purposes and audiences in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive, analytical and/or critical
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and publish texts developing ideas critically, selecting features for complex purposes and audiences.

standards.title: Deliver analytical presentations
standards.description: Plan, create, rehearse and deliver spoken and multimodal presentations for purpose and audience, using language features, literary devices and features of voice such as volume, tone, pitch and pace, and organising, expanding and developing ideas in ways that may be imaginative, reflective, informative, persuasive, analytical and/or critical
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students plan, create and deliver presentations developing ideas analytically and critically for complex purposes.

standards.title: Representations across contexts
standards.description: Analyse the representations of people and places in literary texts, drawn from historical, social and cultural contexts, by First Nations Australian, and wide-ranging Australian and world authors
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how people and places are represented in literary texts across historical, social and cultural contexts.

standards.title: Personal response and analysis
standards.description: Present a personal response to a literary text comparing initial impressions and subsequent analysis of the whole text
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students present personal responses comparing initial impressions with subsequent analysis of whole texts.

standards.title: Features influence preferences
standards.description: Analyse how features of literary texts influence readers' preference for texts
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse how features of literary texts influence reader preferences.

standards.title: Aesthetic qualities of style
standards.description: Analyse texts and evaluate the aesthetic qualities and appeal of an author's literary style
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse texts and evaluate the aesthetic qualities and appeal of an author's literary style.

standards.title: Complex literary devices
standards.description: Analyse the effect of text structures, language features and literary devices such as extended metaphor, metonymy, allegory, symbolism and intertextual references
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students analyse the effect of complex literary devices including extended metaphor, allegory, symbolism and intertextual references.

standards.title: Create hybrid experimental texts
standards.description: Create and edit literary texts, that may be a hybrid, that experiment with text structures, language features and literary devices for purposes and audiences
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students create and edit literary texts including hybrids, experimenting with structures, features and devices for purposes and audiences.

standards.title: Language includes and excludes
standards.description: Understand how language can have inclusive and exclusive social effects, and can empower or disempower people
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand how language can include or exclude, and empower or disempower people.

standards.title: Evaluative language reveals values
standards.description: Understand that language used to evaluate, implicitly or explicitly reveals an individual's values
standards.progression_checkpoint: Students understand that evaluative language implicitly or explicitly reveals an individual's values.

standards.title: Evaluate text structure effectiveness
